title: Apollo’s Legacy: From Moon Race to Artemis
summary: Half a century after Apollo 11, NASA leaders reflect on its lasting impact and the urgent push to return sustainably. The conversation ties historic triumphs to modern geopolitics, personal memories, and the need for a new defining achievement.

clips.title: Buying Services, Not Hardware
clips.why: Highlights the radical procurement change where NASA will pay for a lunar‑landing service instead of building a lander, a surprising move that speeds development.

captions.reels:
💡 NASA is buying a moon‑landing service, not a lander!

Instead of traditional contracts, they’ll pay companies to take astronauts from Gateway to the surface and back.

Tag a friend who loves space tech!
#CommercialSpace #Artemis #Innovation #NASA #Moon
captions.linkedin:
NASA shifts to service‑based procurement for lunar landings.

Rather than owning a lander, the agency will contract a provider to ferry astronauts from Gateway to the Moon and back.

Why it matters: This model cuts years off development and leverages private investment.

Lesson: Outsourcing core capabilities can accelerate innovation and share risk.

Would you adopt a service model in your field?
#CommercialSpace #Strategy
captions.x: NASA will pay for a moon‑landing service, not build the lander itself. #Artemis

clips.title: Gateway to the Moon
clips.why: Introduces the Gateway as a reusable lunar hub that solves the energy gap and expands access, a fresh architecture that excites listeners.

captions.reels:
🌙 Gateway: The Moon’s new space station hub!

Astronauts fly SLS and Orion to a small station orbiting the Moon, then take a lander down to the surface and back.

Follow for more lunar updates!
#Gateway #Artemis #Moon #NASA #SpaceExploration
captions.linkedin:
NASA unveils the Gateway, a lunar orbit station.

The agency plans a reusable command module that will stay for 15 years, providing solar‑electric propulsion and flexible access to the Moon.

Why it matters: It solves the energy gap for returning astronauts home and expands landing sites.

Lesson: Building modular, long‑term infrastructure can unlock new mission capabilities.
